'''Yurahime Shrine''' (由良比女神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Uragō, [[Nishinoshima Town]], [[:en:Oki District|Oki District]], {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}), the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|Ichinomiya|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
The enshrined deity is:
* {{ill|Suseri-Hime|lt=Suseri-Hime|lt=Suserihime|ja|須勢理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suserihime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}}, also locally known as Yurahime Ōkami.

The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} lists the shrine as "Yurahime Shrine, Myōjin Taisha, formerly known as Watasu God." The deity is sometimes associated with {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}} (sea deity). Records such as the {{ill|Shūchūshō|ja|袖中抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sodenaka-shō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97184798}} and {{ill|Tosa Nikki|en|Tosa Nikki|qid=Q844452|lt=Tosa Nikki}} refer to it as the "Chiburi God."

Local folklore recounts that {{ill|Suseri-Hime|lt=Suseri-Hime|lt=Suserihime|ja|須勢理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suserihime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} once crossed the sea in a taro bucket and was pulled by a squid. In atonement, squid reportedly flock to the shrine’s shore every year.

== History ==
=== Early History ===
The shrine's founding date is unknown.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=Rikkokushi}}, {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}} mentions in {{ill|Jōwa|en|Jōwa|qid=Q3577279|lt=Jōwa (era)}} 9 (842 CE) that Yurahime Shrine, {{ill|Ujika Shrine|ja|宇受賀命神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujika Shrine|qq=}} on {{ill|Nakanoshima (disambiguation)|ja|中ノ島|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakanoshima (Shimane)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中之島|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6960286}}, and {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|qid=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} on {{ill|Dōgojima|en|Dōgojima|qid=Q3623017|lt=Dōgo Island}} were designated as official shrines.

The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō (era)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927 CE), lists the shrine as "Yurahime Shrine, Myōjin Taisha, formerly Watasu God." In the {{ill|Oki Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|Oki Province 内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, it is recorded as "Jusanmi no Kami Yurahime Daimyōjin."

After a period of decline during the Middle Ages, the shrine's annual festival was revived in {{ill|An'ei|ja|安永|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/An'ei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 安永 (元号)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1193910}} 2 (1773) by the village leaders of the 13 local villages. In the modern era, it was designated as the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|Ichinomiya|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1872. The current shrine buildings were constructed and expanded beginning in 1889.

=== Divine Rank ===
* Jusanmi (Junior Third Rank) - Listed as "Yurahime Daimyōjin" in the {{ill|Oki Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|Oki Province 内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

== Rituals ==
=== Festivals ===
* Yurahime Shrine festival: Formerly held biennially on July 28–29, it is now celebrated in odd-numbered years on the final Saturday and Sunday of July.<ref>西ノ島町（編集）『隠岐 西ノ島アルバム』[[San'in Chūō Shimbunsha]], p. 157</ref><ref>西ノ島町観光協会『隠岐・西ノ島町』Nishinoshima Town Tourism Association, p. 15</ref>

During the festival, a {{ill|Mikoshi|en|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi}} is placed on a boat formed by linking two large fishing vessels. The mikoshi crosses the sea accompanied by the {{ill|Oki-Dozen Kagura|ja|隠岐島前神楽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki-Dozen Kagura|qq=}} and parades through the town before being brought back to the shrine.<ref name="kawamoto139">{{ill|Kawamoto Mitsunori|ja|川本貢功|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawamoto Mitsunori|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}『隠岐 川本貢功写真集』[[San'in Chūō Shimbunsha]], p. 139</ref>

== Grounds ==
[[File:Yurahime jinja Honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (Town-designated Cultural Property)}}]]
* Main Hall: Built in 1889, featuring modified {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|en|Kasuga-zukuri|qid=Q3193781|lt=Kasuga-zukuri}} architecture with a {{ill|Karahafu|en|Karahafu|qid=Q977293|lt=Karahafu}} gable. The design, formerly described as a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|en|Taisha-zukuri|qid=Q387874|lt=Taisha-zukuri}}, is now referred to as "Kasuga-zukuri variation." The hall is a designated cultural property of Nishinoshima Town.

== Folklore ==
[[File:Precincts of Yurahime jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Yura Beach ("Squid Gathering Beach")}}]]
The shrine's beach is famous for squid that gather annually from October to February, a phenomenon attributed to a legend involving the deity Suserihime and a squid.<ref name="notsu215">{{ill|Notsu Ryū|ja|野津龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Notsu Ryū|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}『隠岐島の伝説』[[Nihon Shashin Shuppan]], pp. 215–216</ref>
